clean_source_blocks.text: Anthropic and SpaceX strike a sweeping compute deal even as Musk takes shots at the company. Anthropic has announced a major new computing partnership with SpaceX, giving the artificial intelligence company access to the full capacity of a massive data center in Memphis, Tennessee a deal that arrives despite a very public feud between Anthropic and SpaceX owner Elon Musk. The agreement grants Anthropic access to more than 300 megawatts of compute capacity at SpaceX’s Colossus 1 facility, currently one of the largest AI data centers in the country. According to Anthropic, the deal will directly benefit subscribers of its paid Claude Pro and Claude Max tiers, expanding the computing resources available to power its Claude family of AI models. ---

See more of our coverage in your search results. SpaceX said Wednesday it would lease its Colossus 1 artificial intelligence data center to Anthropic, pairing Elon Musk’s company with a previously criticized rival in a deal that could add momentum to the Claude creator’s AI coding push. Under the agreement, Anthropic will use the full computing power of the facility in Memphis, Tennessee, which houses more than 220,000 Nvidia processors and will give the Claude chatbot maker 300 megawatts of new capacity within a month. The deal gives Musk’s IPO-bound SpaceX a marquee customer as it looks to sell investors on its AI ambitions while helping Anthropic ease capacity constraints following surging demand for products such as its AI coding tool, Claude Code.

The company said it is also interested in working with SpaceX to develop multiple gigawatts of space-based orbital data centers – one of Musk’s key goals and a major driver behind SpaceX’s initial public offering, as the endeavor is expected to be highly capital intensive and technically challenging. In a statement on X, Musk said that he made the decision to lease computing power after spending time with Anthropic leaders last week. Their work to ensure Anthropic’s Claude AI is “good for humanity” impressed him, he said. “No one set off my evil detector,” wrote Musk, who is battling OpenAI and its CEO Sam Altman in court for allegedly breaching its mission to develop AI for the good of humanity.

SpaceX said Wednesday it would lease its Colossus 1 artificial intelligence data center to Anthropic, pairing Elon Musk’s company with a previously criticized rival in a deal that could add momentum to the Claude creator’s AI coding push.

Under the agreement, Anthropic will use the full computing power of the facility in Memphis, Tennessee, which houses more than 220,000 Nvidia processors and will give the Claude chatbot maker 300 megawatts of new capacity within a month.

The deal gives Musk’s IPO-bound SpaceX a marquee customer as it looks to sell investors on its AI ambitions while helping Anthropic ease capacity constraints following surging demand for products such as its AI coding tool, Claude Code.

The announcement came as Anthropic held a developer day in San Francisco on Wednesday, where it unveiled a new Claude AI feature called “dreaming” that is meant to help its AI systems learn by reviewing work between sessions, spotting patterns and updating files that store user preferences and other context.

Buoyed by the extra capacity from the SpaceX deal and other similar recent agreements, Anthropic said it was doubling Claude Code’s rate limits for its paid plans, removing peak-hour usage caps for Pro and Max accounts and sharply increasing the volume of requests developers can make to its Claude Opus models.

The company said it is also interested in working with SpaceX to develop multiple gigawatts of space-based orbital data centers – one of Musk’s key goals and a major driver behind SpaceX’s initial public offering, as the endeavor is expected to be highly capital intensive and technically challenging.

In a statement on X, Musk said that he made the decision to lease computing power after spending time with Anthropic leaders last week. Their work to ensure Anthropic’s Claude AI is “good for humanity” impressed him, he said.

“No one set off my evil detector,” wrote Musk, who is battling OpenAI and its CEO Sam Altman in court for allegedly breaching its mission to develop AI for the good of humanity.

[Lähde: Rolling Out]
Anthropic and SpaceX strike a sweeping compute deal even as Musk takes shots at the company. Anthropic has announced a major new computing partnership with SpaceX, giving the artificial intelligence company access to the full capacity of a massive data center in Memphis, Tennessee a deal that arrives despite a very public feud between Anthropic and SpaceX owner Elon Musk.

The agreement grants Anthropic access to more than 300 megawatts of compute capacity at SpaceX’s Colossus 1 facility, currently one of the largest AI data centers in the country. According to Anthropic, the deal will directly benefit subscribers of its paid Claude Pro and Claude Max tiers, expanding the computing resources available to power its Claude family of AI models.

---

[Lähde: 24/7 Wall St]
The excitement surrounding the IPO of Elon Musk’s SpaceX is almost palpable at this point. The largest IPO the world has ever seen could surely make a splash in the first days, weeks, and months following the landing.

I have no idea what the day-one valuation will be, but it feels like the many followers of Elon Musk might be committed, regardless of how heated. In any case, the SpaceX IPO seems to be very well-timed, with the Nasdaq 100 going into overdrive, spiking to hit a new all-time high on Friday as investors applauded the good jobs number.

With recent news breaking that Anthropic, which has arguably pulled quite far ahead in the AI race, will lease the entirety of the Colossus 1 supercluster (and yes, it’s as big as it sounds, with more than 220,000 Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA | NVDA Price Prediction) GPUs and plenty of power), I do think that we’re witnessing a very favorably transition as Elon Musk does business with a rival he may have been critical of just a few months ago. Either way, there’s no reason why great rivals cannot also be great allies, especially given the stakes on the line for America in this great AI race.

The co-opetition (co-operation and competition) model may very well be what helps the U.S. pull further ahead as firms work together to advance their efforts, but also compete in a fiercely competitive market. If the AI revolution is as big as investors think, though, I do think that there’s an abundance of rewards to go around, and that makes the case for more alliances. The same goes for circular deals, which ultimately might help the cause with fewer inefficiencies.

So, what makes the latest Anthropic deal with Elon Musk’s firm such a big deal?

With Elon Musk going at it with OpenAI in an ongoing trial, perhaps it’s best that Musk and his companies stand in Anthropic’s corner, which is the top rival of Sam Altman’s OpenAI. Is the rival of a rival actually a friend?

payload.title: Musk kuvaa Anthropicin SpaceX-sopimusta lyhyeksi, vaikka asiakirjat viittaavat pidempään maksujaksoon
payload.summary: SpaceX on sopinut vuokraavansa Memphisissä sijaitsevan Colossus 1 -tekoälydatakeskuksensa laskentakapasiteettia Anthropicille, mutta sopimuksen kestosta on syntynyt epäselvyyttä Elon Muskin julkisten kommenttien ja SpaceX:n oman listautumisaineiston välillä.
payload.content:
SpaceX on sopinut antavansa Anthropicin käyttöön Memphisissä Tennesseessä sijaitsevan Colossus 1 -tekoälydatakeskuksen laskentakapasiteettia. Järjestely on poikkeuksellinen, koska Elon Musk on aiemmin arvostellut Anthropicia julkisesti, mutta kuvaa nyt yhtiön kanssa tehtyä sopimusta myönteisemmin ja samalla lyhytaikaiseksi sekä peruutettavissa olevaksi.

## Suuri kapasiteettisopimus Memphisissä

Sopimuksen mukaan Anthropic saa käyttöönsä yli 300 megawattia laskentakapasiteettia Colossus 1 -keskuksesta. Keskuksen kerrotaan sisältävän yli 220 000 Nvidian prosessoria, ja lisäkapasiteetin on määrä tulla Anthropicin käyttöön noin kuukauden kuluessa.

Anthropicille järjestely voi helpottaa kapasiteettipulaa tilanteessa, jossa Claude-tuoteperheen kysyntä on kasvanut. Yhtiön mukaan lisälaskenta tukee erityisesti maksullisia Claude Pro- ja Claude Max -tilaajia sekä laajemmin Claude-mallien käyttöä. Kysyntää on lisännyt myös Claude Code, ohjelmistokehitykseen suunnattu tekoälytyökalu.

SpaceX:lle sopimus tuo näkyvän asiakkaan sen tekoälyinfrastruktuurille. Samalla se tukee yhtiön pyrkimystä vakuuttaa sijoittajia tekoälyyn liittyvistä kasvumahdollisuuksista listautumissuunnitelmien yhteydessä.

## Sopimuksen kestosta eri viestejä

Sopimuksen pituus on noussut keskeiseksi kysymykseksi. Musk on julkisesti kuvannut järjestelyä lyhytaikaiseksi ja peruutettavissa olevaksi. SpaceX:n omassa listautumisaineistossa taas kuvataan maksuja toukokuuhun 2029 saakka, mikä antaa pidemmän aikavälin kuvan järjestelyn taloudellisesta vaikutuksesta.

Musk kertoi päätyneensä vuokraamaan kapasiteettia vietettyään aikaa Anthropicin johdon kanssa. Hänen mukaansa vaikutuksen teki yhtiön työ sen eteen, että Claude-tekoäly olisi ihmiskunnalle hyödyllinen. Kommentit merkitsevät selvää sävynmuutosta, sillä Musk syytti vielä helmikuussa Anthropicin tekoälyä vinoumista.

Musk on myös sanonut, että SpaceX on siirtänyt omat tekoälyn koulutustarpeensa Colossus 2 -keskukseen. Hänen mukaansa yhtiö voisi tarjota kapasiteettia muillekin tekoäly-yhtiöille, jos ne pyrkivät samanlaisiin ihmiskuntaa hyödyttäviin tavoitteisiin.

Anthropic ja SpaceX ovat lisäksi kertoneet kiinnostuksesta kehittää avaruuteen sijoitettavia datakeskuksia, joiden kapasiteetti voisi tulevaisuudessa nousta useisiin gigawatteihin. Hanke olisi teknisesti vaikea ja pääomavaltainen, mutta se sopii Muskin pitkän aikavälin visioon SpaceX:n roolista tekoälyinfrastruktuurissa.
summary_bullets: Anthropic saa käyttöönsä yli 300 megawattia SpaceX:n Colossus 1 -datakeskuksen kapasiteettia Memphisissä.
Elon Musk kuvaa sopimusta lyhytaikaiseksi ja peruutettavissa olevaksi, vaikka SpaceX:n aineistossa viitataan maksuihin toukokuuhun 2029 saakka.
Sopimus voi helpottaa Anthropicin kapasiteettipulaa ja vahvistaa SpaceX:n tekoälyinfrastruktuuriin liittyvää sijoittajatarinaa.

Hanke olisi teknisesti vaikea ja pääomavaltainen, mutta se sopii Muskin pitkän aikavälin visioon SpaceX:n roolista tekoälyinfrastruktuurissa.

article.source_text:
Anthropic and SpaceX strike a sweeping compute deal even as Musk takes shots at the company. Anthropic has announced a major new computing partnership with SpaceX, giving the artificial intelligence company access to the full capacity of a massive data center in Memphis, Tennessee a deal that arrives despite a very public feud between Anthropic and SpaceX owner Elon Musk. The agreement grants Anthropic access to more than 300 megawatts of compute capacity at SpaceX’s Colossus 1 facility, currently one of the largest AI data centers in the country. According to Anthropic, the deal will directly benefit subscribers of its paid Claude Pro and Claude Max tiers, expanding the computing resources available to power its Claude family of AI models. ---

See more of our coverage in your search results. SpaceX said Wednesday it would lease its Colossus 1 artificial intelligence data center to Anthropic, pairing Elon Musk’s company with a previously criticized rival in a deal that could add momentum to the Claude creator’s AI coding push. Under the agreement, Anthropic will use the full computing power of the facility in Memphis, Tennessee, which houses more than 220,000 Nvidia processors and will give the Claude chatbot maker 300 megawatts of new capacity within a month. The deal gives Musk’s IPO-bound SpaceX a marquee customer as it looks to sell investors on its AI ambitions while helping Anthropic ease capacity constraints following surging demand for products such as its AI coding tool, Claude Code.

The company said it is also interested in working with SpaceX to develop multiple gigawatts of space-based orbital data centers – one of Musk’s key goals and a major driver behind SpaceX’s initial public offering, as the endeavor is expected to be highly capital intensive and technically challenging. In a statement on X, Musk said that he made the decision to lease computing power after spending time with Anthropic leaders last week. Their work to ensure Anthropic’s Claude AI is “good for humanity” impressed him, he said. “No one set off my evil detector,” wrote Musk, who is battling OpenAI and its CEO Sam Altman in court for allegedly breaching its mission to develop AI for the good of humanity.
